speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) how does the Ministry determine the frequency of its safety inspections of MRT train operators; (b) what is the expected scope of such safety inspections; and (c) whether the Ministry conducts surprise safety inspections on train operators and, if so, where can the results of such inspections be found.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: They should also take reasonably practicable measures to ensure the safety and health of their workers.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This is enforced under the Workplace Safety and Health Act.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: In short, more inspections are conducted for higher-risk activities and fewer inspections for lower-risk activities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: This is to avoid disruption to train operations during commuting hours as well as the need to obtain security clearance to enter the train depots and track areas safely.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: An inspection report of any identified safety lapses will be shared with the companies for remedial actions to be taken.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Findings and learning points from the inspections are shared with the industry stakeholders while preserving the confidentiality of the inspected companies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Sharing of the learning points is to create greater awareness and also to enable more companies to adopt safer workplace practices to improve workplace safety and health conditions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In an answer to my colleague hon Member Assoc Prof Daniel Goh's question last month, MOM said, "Our inspection focus on work at height activities and falling object hazards which were the main causes of workplace fatalities during that period".

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This is for MOM conducting workplace safety inspections of various train depots.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I have also asked about what is the expected scope of such safety inspections.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can I just clarify with the Minister of State that even the recent incident in March 2016, which did not involve work at height activities and falling objects, will MOM be increasing the scope of inspection for MRT train operators?

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: Therefore, the focus of the inspections on MRT had been on some other areas which have a higher risk of dangers to workers.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: In 2016 alone, we had conducted six very in-depth inspections.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: We believe that, together with the MRT management, we have uncovered some unauthorised deviations from the safety procedures.

speaker: Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong
text: From all these additional inspections, we believe that it will help to increase the safety standards in MRT operations.
